brief.headline: commit 367c64a5ae27 rounds refund amounts up, overpaying orders with cents

sentences.text: Commit 367c64a5ae27 is the culprit: at checkpoint 414aea6e5e59 the agent was asked to make issue_refund "round the amount to the nearest whole unit before recording it", and step 65a1490b applied that by replacing `amount` with `round(amount)` in the refund dict, which rounds 64.75 up to 65.
In failing run 142e0dd3a8ed, span 0127ef29 shows issue_refund received amount 64.75 and returned {"refunded":65,"order_id":"5005"}, overpaying by $0.25.
In passing run c67199a025b5 at parent commit 0d8eb7150bfa, span ad7edb7e shows the same input 64.75 returned {"refunded":64.75,"order_id":"5005"} with no rounding.
The bisect measured 12 of 12 replays failing from commit 367c64a5ae27 onward and 0 of 9 failing before it; it failed in all 12 observed replays from the culprit on.

The request asked for rounding so that logged amounts match what the provider pays, but the commit rounds the stored refund amount itself, causing the recorded payout to diverge from the true order amount whenever the order has a non-zero cents component.
